analysis:
All three changed files are documentation only: docs/architecture/inference.md (new 'Native Flint' section, head lines 1717-1843), docs/architecture/model-registry.md (new 'Flint shard-only local discovery' section, head lines 77-90) and docs/developer/build.md (new Flint build steps). No executable code, configuration or deployment change is in the supplied units, so no control from the threat model is altered by this PR itself.

The documented behavior does touch a few boundaries, and the next pass should check the real source for each:
- Discovery (TB-003, T-012, A-004): the shard-only Flint exception in ModelScanner.isMLXModel is described as bounded (config nonempty, at most 1,048,576 bytes, nonblocking open, regular-file check, exact 'flint' architecture). It states that tensor completeness is not verified at discovery and is left to the native loader and on-demand hasher. The source was not supplied, so whether weight hashing and verification actually run before serving, and whether an operator can substitute weights (T-012, T-027), is unverified.
- Tool-call framing (TB-007): FlintNativeProtocolConstraint is described as an envelope constraint, with full JSON/schema post-validation kept in the .flint parser and ToolConstraintValidation. The documentation says malformed frames fail closed. Not verified against source.
- Prefix cache (T-041): the documentation says the Flint prefix policy, KV precision and SSD behavior are unchanged, and only native KV and checkpoint precision are required. Whether Flint participates in the encrypted SSD tier is not stated. No change to the TTL, HMAC lookup tags or cacheSalt scoping is documented.
- Context bounds (T-010 availability): admission is described as HTTP 400 before SSE headers when prompt plus output budget exceeds the loaded config context.
- Build (A-011, T-013): the build.md change pins submodule commits for libs/mlx-swift-lm and libs/mlx-swift. It does not alter release registration or the binary hash registry. The listed environment variables only select native KV and checkpoint precision.

No security regression is identified from documentation alone. Cross-checking the documented claims against the actual Swift sources (ModelScanner, FlintNativeProtocolConstraint, the loader) was not possible with the supplied evidence.
